extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literature; aspiring writers; literary critics; people interested in the social role of books and authors
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for what makes a genuine 'Man of Letters' (the literary hero): his moral/intellectual qualities, social function, relationship to truth and society, and the ordeals/conditions that test genuineness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living in the Divine Idea / originality, sincerity, genius
rubrics_metrics.description: The Man of Letters 'lives in the inward sphere of things, in the True, Divine and Eternal' — what we call 'originality,' 'sincerity,' 'genius'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fichte's test: whoever does not 'live wholly in this Divine Idea' or struggles not to live wholly in it is no Literary Man — a 'Bungler, Stumper' or 'Nonentity.' The text treats 'inspired' authenticity (not mere professional success) as the defining standard of a genuine literary hero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function as Prophet/Priest (revelation of the Godlike)
rubrics_metrics.description: The literary hero's role is prophetic/priestly: to discern and make manifest the 'Divine Idea of the World' — to unfold the Godlike to men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seen as a continual Priesthood: the Man of Letters 'is the light of the world; the world's Priest;--guiding it, like a sacred Pillar of Fire.' The standard of value is whether the writer reveals what lies beneath mere appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful reporting / accuracy of the writer's 'eye'
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers must not 'report falsely' — the 'eye' must not 'report not falsely', because books influence how other social organs (teaching, governing, worship) function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books are the vehicles by which the Past and Distant relate to the Present; thus accuracy, fidelity to truth and reality, and not misrepresentation, are essential. Anti-pattern: careless, misleading writing that misinforms readers and misguides society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature as 'apocalypse of Nature' / capacity to reveal and uplift
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature should be a 'revealing of the open secret' — a continuous revelation of the Godlike in the terrestrial and common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation emphasizes whether writing brings the reader to a clearer, higher perception (aesthetic or moral), e.g., making 'a lily of the fields' appear as an effluence of the Fountain of all Beauty. Works that move hearts into something like worship are highly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal reach and longevity (writing for all times and places)
rubrics_metrics.description: A true Man of Letters writes not merely 'to this parish or that, on this day or that, but to all men in all times and places' — books should speak across time and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The value of a book is judged by its ability to address universal human concerns and to endure: the 'soul of the Past' survives in preserved books. Works that teach generations are preferred to ephemeral writings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to persuade and shape public life (the Fourth Estate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers and printed speech function as a kind of Church and a 'Fourth Estate' — they wield real influence in law-making, governance, and public morals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes the extent to which an author's output effectively shapes public opinion, moral sentiment, or political discourse. With influence comes responsibility: invention of writing implies a democratic power that must be exercised conscientiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuineness tested by poverty and ordeal (resistance to worldly gain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuine literary heroism is often forged in poverty and struggle; poverty can be beneficial to the Man of Letters as a test of sincerity and resistance to pride or vanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that stipends/endowments alone cannot make a true writer. The 'wild welter of a chaos' of literary life is an 'ordeal' that must be passed; seeking money, pride, or success as primary aims is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of superficial, popular or spurious writing (not a 'Bungler' or 'Hodman')
rubrics_metrics.description: There are genuine and spurious Men of Letters: the latter are superficial, unheroic, and not living in the Divine Idea; Fichte labels them 'Bungler, Stumper' or 'Nonentity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should distinguish deep, original, sincere work from mere professional, prosaic, or fashionable writing. Anti-patterns include writing merely to amuse, to flatter, or for ephemeral market success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social organization and support vs chaotic neglect
rubrics_metrics.description: Society should not leave literary life to 'Chaos'; the organization, recognition, and proper arrangements for the Literary Class are necessary (but mere money-grants are not the full solution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include whether institutions (universities, public recognition, channels of patronage) identify and fairly advance true literary talent. The text warns against random neglect (e.g., 'your royal Johnson languishing inactive in garrets') and calls for systemic solutions rather than ad hoc charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to oppose falsehood and disorder (moral courage)
rubrics_metrics.description: A hero (and by extension a Man of Letters) must resist falsehood and disorder: 'We are here to resist, to control and vanquish withal... to extinguish Falsehoods.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation values moral courage and the willingness to rebuke error and corruption. This may include uncompromising critique and reformist zeal; tolerance has limits when truth and order are at stake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of Teaching and Speech alongside Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: While writing is supreme, speech (preaching, teaching) still has a distinct and valuable province; the true University and the literary function must integrate books and speech properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether an author's work complements oral teaching and whether institutional structures (universities, schools) are adapting to the primacy of books. The 'true University of these days is a Collection of Books' — evaluation includes how well writers and institutions make knowledge accessible via books.
